intro_html: Char siu is that sweet, glossy Chinese barbecue pork you see hanging in restaurant windows, and here it comes out of the slow cooker for pennies. Each bowl runs 55 grams of protein over rice and broccoli at just $3.61 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings from one batch is a steal you will want on repeat.
cost_closing_html: About $3.61 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: You get about 562 calories and 55 grams of protein in every serving.
upsell_html: Restaurant flavor, home-cook price. Once you taste it you are hooked. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Hoisin sauce is the secret to that char siu taste. One jar lasts through several recipes, so buy it once and it earns its shelf space.
Stick with pork loin over tenderloin here. It stays juicy through the long cook and cuts your protein cost nearly in half.
Honey in the squeeze bottle keeps forever and you only need a few tablespoons, so it barely dents this recipe's cost.
make_it: Lay the pork loin in the slow cooker.
Stir together the hoisin sauce, soy sauce, honey, and chicken broth, then pour it over.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork is fall-apart tender.
Shred the pork and stir it back through the glaze.
Steam the broccoli florets until bright green and just tender.
Serve over cooked white rice with the broccoli alongside and pack it up.
